content: Sarecycline is indicated for the treatment of inflammatory lesions associated with non-nodular moderate-to-severe acne. The recommended dosage is weight-based: for patients under 54 kg, 60 mg orally once daily; for those weighing 55–84 kg, 100 mg orally once daily; and for those weighing 85–136 kg, 150 mg orally once daily. If no improvement is observed after 12 weeks of treatment, the therapy should be reassessed. The safety and efficacy of sarecycline in patients under 9 years of age have not been established. Concomitant use of sarecycline with acitretin is contraindicated due to an increased risk of toxicity, although the mechanism is unknown. Similarly, combining oral retinoids with tetracyclines, including sarecycline, may elevate the risk of pseudotumor cerebri (intracranial hypertension). Sarecycline may reduce the effectiveness of amoxicillin, ampicillin, dicloxacillin, nafcillin, oxacillin, penicillin G (aqueous, benzathine, or procaine), penicillin VK, and piperacillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Tetracyclines, in general, can interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. If these drugs are used together, monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins. Alternative therapies should be considered when possible. Sarecycline can increase the effects of neuromuscular blocking agents such as atracurium, cisatracurium, pancuronium, rocuronium, succinylcholine, and vecuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, which may lead to respiratory depression. Avoid or use alternative drugs in such cases. The combination of sarecycline with retinoids like bexarotene, isotretinoin, tretinoin, or palovarotene should be avoided due to an increased risk of toxicity and pseudotumor cerebri. Sarecycline may reduce the efficacy of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid administering the vaccine to patients who have received systemic antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. Sarecycline can increase the levels or effects of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) substrates, including abemaciclib, afatinib, aliskiren, ambrisentan, amiodarone, amitriptyline, apixaban, atorvastatin, bendamustine, betrixaban, brentuximab vedotin, budesonide, carfilzomib, carvedilol, ceritinib, cetirizine, crizotinib, cyclosporine, dabigatran, dabrafenib, dasabuvir, daunorubicin, desloratadine, dexamethasone, digoxin, diltiazem, docetaxel, doxorubicin, duvelisib, edoxaban, eletriptan, erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, or stearate), everolimus, and others. Use caution and monitor for toxicities, as dosage adjustments may be required. Multivalent cation-containing products, such as aluminum hydroxide, magnesium carbonate, magnesium trisilicate, calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, calcium gluconate, calcium/vitamin D, carbonyl iron, ferric carboxymaltose, ferric citrate, ferric gluconate, ferric maltol, ferric pyrophosphate dialysate, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, ferrous sulfate, and others, can decrease the absorption and efficacy of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. To avoid this interaction, administer tetracyclines at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these products. Bile acid sequestrants, such as cholestyramine, colesevelam, and colestipol, may also reduce the absorption and efficacy of sarecycline. Separate dosing by at least 2 hours if coadministration is necessary. Chromium and copper can similarly impair sarecycline absorption. Monitor closely and separate dosing to minimize interactions. Sarecycline may increase the levels or effects of drugs like cimetidine, ciprofloxacin, and others that are P-gp substrates. Monitor for toxicities and adjust dosages as needed.
